_notes: Real, published CVEs (verified against NVD/vendor advisories as of Aug 2026). Matching is by open PORT/SERVICE NAME only - this tool does not fingerprint exact software versions, so a match means 'this service is open and could be running vulnerable software', not a confirmed vulnerability. Always verify the actual software version on the target before treating a match as confirmed.

SSH.title: regreSSHion - OpenSSH Signal Handler Race Condition RCE
SSH.description: Unauthenticated remote code execution as root via a race condition in sshd's SIGALRM handler when a client fails to authenticate within LoginGraceTime. Regression of CVE-2006-5051.

remediation.title: Update OpenSSH to 9.8p1 or later
steps: Check current version: ssh -V
Update via package manager (apt/yum/dnf) or compile OpenSSH >= 9.8p1
If patching isn't immediately possible, set LoginGraceTime 0 in sshd_config as a temporary mitigation (note: this exposes a DoS risk)
Restart sshd: systemctl restart sshd
Verify version again with ssh -V

FTP.title: vsftpd 2.3.4 Backdoor Command Execution
FTP.description: A backdoor was injected into the vsftpd 2.3.4 source tarball. A specific string sent during login opens a root shell on TCP port 6200.

remediation.title: Verify vsftpd is not the backdoored 2.3.4 build
steps: Check version: vsftpd -v or check installed package version
If running the compromised 2.3.4 build, immediately update to a current vsftpd release from your distro's repo
Check for an unexpected listener on TCP port 6200
Review FTP server and system logs for signs of prior compromise
Restart the FTP service after updating

RDP.title: BlueKeep - Windows RDP Remote Code Execution
RDP.description: Pre-authentication, wormable RCE in Remote Desktop Services. No user interaction or credentials required. Actively exploited in the wild.

remediation.title: Patch Windows RDP (MS security update) or disable RDP
steps: Install the May 2019 Microsoft security update (or later cumulative update) covering CVE-2019-0708
If patching isn't possible, disable Remote Desktop Services entirely, or restrict RDP (port 3389) to a VPN/jump host only
Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) as a partial mitigation
Block port 3389 at the perimeter firewall for any system exposed to the internet
Confirm patch status via Windows Update history

SMB.title: EternalBlue - SMBv1 Remote Code Execution
SMB.description: Remote code execution in the SMBv1 server via crafted packets. Used by the WannaCry and NotPetya worms to spread globally in 2017.

remediation.title: Disable SMBv1 and apply MS17-010
steps: Apply the MS17-010 security update / latest cumulative Windows update
Disable the SMBv1 protocol: Windows Features > SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support > uncheck
Or via PowerShell: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol
Block TCP 445 at the network perimeter for internet-facing systems
Confirm SMBv1 is disabled with Get-SmbServerConfiguration

HTTP.title: Log4Shell - Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution
affected: Any Java web app using Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1
HTTP.description: Unauthenticated RCE via JNDI lookups in log messages. One of the most widely exploited vulnerabilities ever disclosed; affects any web app on this port built on vulnerable Log4j2 versions, not the web server software itself.

remediation.title: Upgrade Log4j2 to 2.17.1+ (or later per app stack)
steps: Identify whether the web application uses Log4j2 and which version (check WEB-INF/lib or build dependencies)
Upgrade to Log4j2 2.17.1 or later for Java 8+ (or the appropriate patched line for older Java)
If upgrading isn't immediately possible, set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true or remove the JndiLookup class from the classpath as a mitigation
Restart the application after patching
Scan outbound logs/WAF for JNDI/LDAP exploitation attempts to check for prior compromise

HTTPS.title: Log4Shell - Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution
affected: Any Java web app using Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.14.1
HTTPS.description: Unauthenticated RCE via JNDI lookups in log messages, same as the HTTP entry - relevant to any TLS-terminated Java web app on this port.

remediation.title: Upgrade Log4j2 to 2.17.1+ (or later per app stack)
steps: Identify whether the web application uses Log4j2 and which version
Upgrade to Log4j2 2.17.1 or later
Mitigate with log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true if an immediate upgrade isn't possible
Restart the application after patching
Check logs/WAF for exploitation attempts

Telnet.title: Telnet Transmits Credentials and Data in Cleartext
affected: All Telnet servers by protocol design
Telnet.description: Telnet has no built-in encryption. Credentials, commands, and session data are all sent in plaintext and can be captured by anyone on the network path. Not a single CVE - this is an inherent protocol weakness, which is why Telnet is considered obsolete for anything but isolated legacy/serial console use.

remediation.title: Disable Telnet and use SSH instead
steps: Disable the Telnet service/daemon on the device
Enable SSH as a replacement if the device supports it
If Telnet must remain (e.g. legacy hardware), restrict access to an isolated management VLAN only
Never use Telnet across untrusted or internet-facing networks

MongoDB.title: MongoDB Running Without Authentication Enabled
affected: MongoDB instances with authorization not enabled (common default in older/self-hosted setups)
MongoDB.description: Older or misconfigured MongoDB deployments bind to all interfaces with no authentication required, allowing anyone who can reach the port to read/write/delete all data. This caused mass ransomware-style database wipes ('Mongo lock' attacks) starting in 2017. Not a single CVE - it's a common dangerous misconfiguration.

remediation.title: Enable authentication and bind to localhost/private network only
steps: Enable access control: set security.authorization: enabled in mongod.conf
Create an admin user with a strong password before restarting with auth enabled
Bind MongoDB to localhost or an internal-only interface (bindIp), not 0.0.0.0
Add firewall rules restricting TCP 27017 to trusted hosts only
Restart mongod and verify unauthenticated connections are refused

Elasticsearch.title: Elasticsearch Exposed Without Authentication
affected: Elasticsearch clusters with security features disabled (common in versions before 8.x default-on security)
Elasticsearch.description: Elasticsearch historically shipped with no authentication by default. Instances exposed to the network without security enabled allow full read/write access to all indexed data and have been repeatedly targeted for data theft and ransom wipes.

remediation.title: Enable Elasticsearch security features and restrict network exposure
steps: Enable xpack.security.enabled: true in elasticsearch.yml (default-on in 8.x+)
Set up authentication (built-in users or your identity provider) and TLS for transport/HTTP layers
Bind to a private network interface, not a publicly routable one
Add firewall rules restricting TCP 9200/9300 to trusted hosts
Restart the cluster and verify unauthenticated requests are rejected

VNC.title: VNC Server With Weak/No Authentication
affected: VNC servers configured with no password or weak legacy DES-based authentication
VNC.description: Many VNC implementations default to weak authentication or none at all, and traffic is often unencrypted, giving full remote desktop control to anyone who can reach the port.

remediation.title: Set a strong VNC password and tunnel over SSH/VPN
steps: Set a strong VNC password (avoid legacy 8-character DES-based auth if a stronger scheme is available)
Tunnel VNC traffic over SSH or a VPN instead of exposing it directly
Restrict access to TCP 5900 via firewall rules to trusted hosts only
Disable VNC entirely if remote desktop access isn't actively needed

MySQL.title: MySQL Exposed to Untrusted Networks
affected: MySQL/MariaDB instances bound to a public or untrusted-reachable interface
MySQL.description: Database servers reachable from untrusted networks are a common entry point for credential-stuffing and brute-force attacks, and increase the blast radius of any future MySQL CVE. This is a generic exposure finding, not a specific CVE - check the actual MySQL/MariaDB version against current CVEs separately.

remediation.title: Restrict MySQL to trusted hosts and check for outstanding patches
steps: Bind MySQL to localhost or a private network interface (bind-address) unless remote access is explicitly required
Restrict TCP 3306 via firewall rules to known application servers only
Check the running MySQL/MariaDB version with SELECT VERSION(); and compare against your vendor's current CVE advisories
Enforce strong passwords and disable unused default accounts
Apply the latest minor version security patches
